world_build — DRIVE world op

• Data kinds: table → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.world_build(course, *, props=(), kerb_height: 'float' = 0.15, kerb_width: 'float' = 0.3, lines: 'bool' = True, ground_margin: 'float' = 8.0, ground_step: 'float' = 4.0, joint_step: 'float' = 0.5, asset_root=None) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import driveworld; driveworld.world_build(course, *, props=(), kerb_height: 'float' = 0.15, kerb_width: 'float' = 0.3, lines: 'bool' = True, ground_margin: 'float' = 8.0, ground_step: 'float' = 4.0, joint_step: 'float' = 0.5, asset_root=None) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("world_build"))

Usage

Builds a world from a course (element or layout).

Road surface = a plane covering everything (z = 0, label 0). Kerbs along the polygon edges of each element (label 1, excluding seam edges), and white lines 0.15 m inside the edges (label 9). Slopes are sloped meshes (label 0). Traffic signals are erected at the intersection's signal_poses (initial state "red", Japanese style: a pole on the far side + an arm carrying a horizontal 3-lamp head over the lane, roadjp), stop lines at stop_lines, and zebra stripes at crosswalks. props is a sequence of (asset_name, x, y, yaw) or (asset_name, x, y, yaw[, dims[, paint]]) (paint = car body colour, CAR_PAINTS). Returns {"V","F","face_label","face_color","objects","bounds","course"}.

Empty input (course an empty dict) raises ValueError.
